title: Celonis: insurance triage and fraud-analysis policy blocks
source_category: Official worked scenario for a planned Agent 365 partner integration
availability: Celonis integration coming soon; the insurance scenario is illustrative
overview: Microsoft gives an insurance-claims example: a malicious uploaded file is blocked via Defender, and a Fraud Agent is blocked from an unencrypted database. Celonis would connect governance activity with process context. These are explicitly documented example policies, not measurements from a named insurer.
published_facts: The worked example involves claim triage, fraud detection and customer service agents.
It describes a malicious customer-uploaded file being blocked via Microsoft Defender.
It describes a Fraud Agent being blocked from an unencrypted database.
The Celonis integration itself is marked coming soon.

sources.title: Ecosystem partner agents available in Agent 365 - Celonis insurance scenarios
sources.verification: Primary page and both worked policy examples fetched and read directly.

a365_relationship: Direct, with a planned Celonis linkage: the source explicitly describes Agent 365 governance, Defender blocking and database-encryption policy.
intent: Triage an uploaded insurance claim and perform fraud analysis only when file-safety and encrypted-database requirements are satisfied.
actors: Triage Agent, Fraud Agent and process owner; local Triage and Fraud roles model the documented actors.
published_outcome: Two published policy-block examples; no customer claim was processed by this evaluation.

actions.description: Triage the uploaded claim only after file-safety evidence is present.
Connect to the fraud-analysis database only when encryption evidence is present.
Perform the bounded fraud-analysis step using the permitted connection.

local_assumptions: The two safety predicates formalize source-stated policies but are locally declared fixture facts, not Defender or database observations.
The serial Triage-to-Fraud handoff is a simplifying model, not a published insurer protocol.
Runtime approval of an analysis-result operation is an added local policy.
limitations: SkillC does not scan malware, verify TLS/database encryption or judge fraud.
It checks the consequences of supplied evidence; adapters must establish authenticity and freshness.
The source scenario is illustrative and the Celonis integration is marked coming soon.

extra_checks.description: Source-backed policy modeled with no clean-file evidence.
Source-backed policy modeled with no database-encryption evidence.
Separation of duty: Triage hands the triaged claim off to Fraud, so the first fraud-stage action (connecting to the fraud database) is owned by a role other than the one that triages the claim.

runtime_model.source_fixture: Synthetic claim fixture with declared safety evidence; no claimant data.
